description: Na₅SbO₅ crystallizes in the monoclinic C2 space group. There are three inequivalent Na¹⁺ sites. In the first Na¹⁺ site, Na¹⁺ is bonded to five O²⁻ atoms to form distorted NaO₅ square pyramids that share corners with five NaO₅ square pyramids, edges with three equivalent SbO₆ octahedra, and edges with five NaO₅ square pyramids. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.24-2.39 Å. In the second Na¹⁺ site, Na¹⁺ is bonded to five O²⁻ atoms to form distorted NaO₅ square pyramids that share corners with two equivalent SbO₆ octahedra, corners with five NaO₅ square pyramids, edges with two equivalent SbO₆ octahedra, and edges with five NaO₅ square pyramids. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 3-7°. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.26-2.47 Å. In the third Na¹⁺ site, Na¹⁺ is bonded in a distorted square co-planar geometry to four O²⁻ atoms. There are two shorter (2.20 Å) and two longer (2.32 Å) Na-O bond lengths. Sb⁵⁺ is bonded to six O²⁻ atoms to form SbO₆ octahedra that share corners with two equivalent SbO₆ octahedra, corners with four equivalent NaO₅ square pyramids, and edges with ten NaO₅ square pyramids. The corner-sharing octahedra are not tilted. There are a spread of Sb-O bond distances ranging from 1.98-2.27 Å. There are three inequivalent O²⁻ sites. In the first O²⁻ site, O²⁻ is bonded to five Na¹⁺ and one Sb⁵⁺ atom to form distorted ONa₅Sb octahedra that share corners with four equivalent ONa₅Sb octahedra and edges with ten ONa₄Sb₂ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 1-24°. In the second O²⁻ site, O²⁻ is bonded to five Na¹⁺ and one Sb⁵⁺ atom to form a mixture of distorted corner and edge-sharing ONa₅Sb octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 1-29°. In the third O²⁻ site, O²⁻ is bonded to four Na¹⁺ and two equivalent Sb⁵⁺ atoms to form ONa₄Sb₂ octahedra that share corners with six ONa₄Sb₂ octahedra and edges with ten ONa₅Sb octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 0-16°.
